## 2d5acf84dd20

**Issue found: the generator resolves a canonical ambiguity in favor of
bounding-box area while the task title and written solution specify nested
containment depth.** Every canonical object is a nested rectangular frame, so
these rules are observationally equivalent there:

- selected program: sort components by descending bounding-box area and color
  them `2,3,4,...`;
- plausible semantic rule: color by containment depth, outermost `2`, next `3`,
  and so on.

The generated distribution is not nested. Exact emitted input for
`seed=0, sample_index=0, difficulty=easy`:

```text
0000000000100
0000000011100
0000000000000
0000000000000
0000000000000
0001000000000
0011000000000
0001000000000
0001000000000
0000000000000
0000001111110
0000001111110
0000000000000
```

It has three side-by-side components with bounding-box areas `12, 8, 6` and no
containment relations. The selected program colors them `2,3,4`; the
containment-depth rule colors all three outermost components `2`. The outputs
differ on nine cells. Thus the generator teaches an implementation-specific
size ranking and removes the nested-frame morphology that gives the canonical
task its stated meaning.

The reproducer verifies that the containment-depth rival matches every
canonical train/test output and records both outputs for this emitted board in
`checks/audit-manual-evidence.json`.
